Row.Text:
Europe, the Mediterranean and Africa above the Equator, with a true start for every civilization of every age and rivers painted where they really run.
THREE MAPS - Distant Lands: Africa, Scandinavia and Iceland lie across the water - One Landmass: the same geography with nothing distant - Finland joins Russia and Egypt joins the Levant by land - Eurasia Compressed: a separate copy you can reshape without touching the other two Sizes 112x98, 128x112 and 144x126.
TRUE STARTS Every civilization of every age has a fixed home, so pick the one that begins where you want your empire to end up. Only one age is live at a time, so the ages share their cities on purpose. The British line plays out where it happened: begin as Gaul on Lake Geneva, become England on the Thames, end as Great Britain or America. Civilizations with no history in Europe are stand-ins. Each holds a region the map would otherwise leave empty, chosen by terrain and, where it matters, by what the civilization unlocks on.
ANTIQUITY Historical homes: - Rome (Rome) - Gaul (Lausanne): the Helvetii on Lake Geneva - Etruscans (Populonia): the one Etruscan city on the sea, as far from Rome as Etruria reaches - Greece (Thermaic Gulf): the coast of Macedon, north of Athens - Byzantium (Constantinople) - Carthage (Carthage) - Egypt (Memphis) - Assyria (Nineveh) - Babylon (Babylon) - Persia (Susa) - Aksum (Axum) Stand-ins: - Mississippians (Uppsala): mound builders at the royal mounds of Gamla Uppsala - Heian Japan (Dublin): an island court off the mainland - Maurya (Madrid): a large warm peninsula to unify - Han (Kyiv): a great river valley, the Dnieper - Maya (Berlin): the north European plain, where Prussia later rises - Khmer (Bucharest): a river empire on the lower Danube - Silla (Ankara): a mountainous peninsula - Tonga (Syracuse): a seafaring power in the middle of the sea
EXPLORATION Historical homes: - England (London) - Byzantium (Constantinople) - Etruscans (Populonia) - Tuscany (Florence) - Bulgaria (Veliko Tarnovo): capital of the Second Bulgarian Empire - Spain (Madrid) - Normans (Rouen) - Abbasids (Baghdad) - Iceland (Reykjavik) - Mongolia (Sarai on the lower Volga): the Golden Horde - Songhai (Gao) - Pirate Republic (Algiers): the Barbary corsairs Stand-ins: - Sengoku Japan (Copenhagen): feudal lords among the Danish islands - Majapahit (Dublin): an island thalassocracy - Chola (Lisbon): a trading coast facing the ocean - Goryeo (Athens): a peninsula of harbours - Dai Viet (Alexandria): a river mouth, the Nile delta - Inca (Tbilisi): mountain settlements, which the Inca unlock on - Hawaii (Syracuse): island settlements, which Hawaii unlocks on - Shawnee (Warsaw): the forests of the Vistula - Ming (Moscow): a vast continental empire on the Russian rivers
MODERN Historical homes: - Great Britain (London) - America (Dublin): across the water from Britain - French Empire (Paris) - Prussia (Berlin) - Russia (Moscow) - Ottomans (Ankara): leaving Constantinople free to be taken - Qajar (Tehran) - Byzantium (Constantinople) - Etruscans (Populonia) Stand-ins: - Mexico (Seville): the Atlantic side of Iberia - Joseon (Athens): a peninsula - Meiji Japan (Uppsala): an industrialising maritime north - Qing (Vienna): a continental empire on the middle Danube - Siam (Naples): a warm coastal kingdom - Mughals (Warsaw): a great land empire, as the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth was - Nepal (Tbilisi): mountain settlements, which Nepal unlocks on - Buganda (Gondar): highland lakes, which Buganda unlocks on
WORKSHOP CIVILIZATIONS Placed too, if you have them installed: Scythia (Kamianka), Kush (Meroe), Sumer (Ur), Austria-Hungary (Vienna), Dutch Republic (Amsterdam).
EVERYONE ELSE A civilization without a start, or one whose start another player already holds, settles a curated historical site: London and Dublin first, then Kyiv, Uppsala, Fez, Krakow, Trondheim, Copenhagen, Marrakesh and 86 more.
Screenshots and details: https://marcobonechi.github.io/civ7mods/europe-mediterranean/
